summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a complex history including end-stage renal disease post-kidney transplant, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and pulmonary hypertension was admitted for acute dyspnea, generalized weakness, and a mechanical fall. He presented with volume overload (proBNP 6932), worsening pleural effusions, and acute kidney injury. Initial management included IV diuretics and initiation of intermittent hemodialysis via a temporary central line, later transitioned to a tunneled dialysis catheter. A CT chest revealed progressive pulmonary opacities, and blood cultures confirmed Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia, prompting targeted antibiotic therapy with meropenem. The patient also had transient dysarthria, ruled out for acute stroke. Over a 35-day stay, he improved clinically, with resolution of sepsis, stabilization of renal function, and reduced respiratory effort. He was discharged on a plan for outpatient IV antibiotics, maintenance hemodialysis, and close multidisciplinary follow-up.
